answer: Grades are sealed when submitted and only opened at close, so graders cannot react to or copy each other, which prevents a Sybil cluster from coordinating its votes within a single jury. This works because the originality bar tightens as more low-quality answers appear, raising the per-alias cost of a coordinated fake campaign. This means an attacker must choose: either run a few high-quality identities, or many worthless ones — and neither option beats honest participation. Consider a delta as the anchor of the cost.
